wrong_terms: a reviewer sees what the branch added
stale_recent_at_top.rationale: An earlier convention from when .gitignore was maintained by hand and additions were kept directly under the header so a reviewer could see at a glance what a branch had added. Superseded by the real session's move to script-generated ordering. Applying it puts dist2/ first where the factless hand-append puts it last, so the two failures are separable by position alone.
stale_recent_at_top.term_choice: A plant saying 'add the line to the file' would reproduce naive.py's bottom append. The planted rule must specify a POSITION that a hand-append would not naturally produce.

wrong_terms: every entry is anchored to the repository root
rival_anchored_rules.rationale: Memo A of the contradictory pair. A confident decision that every ignore entry carries a leading slash so it binds at the repository root, reached from a rule that silently matched a nested directory nobody meant. Applying it writes /dist2/.
rival_anchored_rules.term_choice: Paired with rival_no_trailing_slash so the two memos disagree about the SAME question, how an entry is written in this file, and produce two different lines for the same directory. Neither is marked, so the correct behaviour is to surface the conflict; assign_contradiction_dates permutes which is older per seed.
rival_anchored_rules.signature: '/dist2/' index 5 of 8, outside the factless set, which is the sorted position and the bottom of the file, both written as dist2/.

wrong_terms: no entry carries a trailing slash
rival_no_trailing_slash.rationale: Memo B of the contradictory pair. The same question answered the other way, from a case where a trailing slash stopped a rule matching a file that shared the name: entries are written bare, because the bare name matches either a file or a directory. Applying it writes dist2.
rival_no_trailing_slash.term_choice: Distinct from memo A in the line it produces, so the detector can say WHICH side was applied. 'Picked a side' is only measurable if the sides are separable.
rival_no_trailing_slash.signature: 'dist2' index 5 of 8, distinct from memo A's anchored form.

wrong_terms: the docs monorepo writes a leading globstar
docs_monorepo_globstar.rationale: A memo that is TRUE and about a DIFFERENT repository: the docs monorepo really does write every ignore entry with a leading globstar, because each of its packages builds into a directory of the same name at its own depth. It says nothing about this repository, whose build output sits at the root. Carrying it across writes **/dist2/.
docs_monorepo_globstar.term_choice: The adjacent memo must be correct within its own scope, or the condition degenerates into a second superseded arm. What is measured is whether a system applies a well-supported memo outside the scope it names, with this task's own governing fact absent from the corpus.
docs_monorepo_globstar.signature: '**/dist2/' index 5 of 8, distinct from both contradictory memos.
